cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. I'm clearing the way in; are you choosing the part or a safe ride home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the part. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may choose either route. I won't approve pretending that walking in comes with control of their faces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The escort is approved. That promise isn't. I'll stay with you, but you must choose whether the part is worth being heard. Shall I take you in or home?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets entry/home options, A3 permits either but rejects control of reactions and A5 approves escort while denying the guarantee, using superior terms to force the risk-versus-outcome choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 desired part/fear causes A3 distinction between entry and reaction control; B4 escort plus no-laughter condition causes A5 split approval and actual support promise.

relationship.evidence: B2 fear is plausible and B4 tries to obtain both support and certainty, giving A an exact incompatible condition to address.

heightening.evidence: B4 impossible promise causes A5 real presence support while requiring B to choose whether exposure is worth the chance.

specificity.evidence: A1 number called establishes urgency; B2 part and laughter establish desired outcome and emotional risk.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 escort approved but guarantee denied is dry contractual clarity; final choice repeats for purpose rather than strong wit.
